messages:
Alex M: seeing elevated 5xx and long queue times for the us-east-1 GPU pool, starting ~1761284380. Gpu-util looks fine, but requests are timing out at the frontend.
Priya S: on it — can you paste the service node health? I’ll check autoscaler logs and the network fabric.
Alex M: kube: 3 nodes NotReady in rack-a-us-east-1a, 2 nodes kubelet crashlooping.
Josh R: grabbing dmesg / var logs now. preliminary: NIC driver errors + OOM kill on runtime-managed processes on those nodes.
SRE-Oncall: Incident created: INC-2026-0233 - us-east-1 GPU capacity degradation. Priority: P1.
DeployBot: @channel routing rule update queued: prefer-region=us-west-2 for model-route: text-generation-prod.
Maya (support): drafting status update for status.redwood.ai. Proposed: "Degraded GPU capacity in us-east-1 affecting latency and connection stability for some customers. Traffic is being routed to other regions while we investigate. ETA 45-60m." Thoughts?
Ben L: good. escalate to sales for top 5 enterprise customers + send heads-up with ETA and mitigation steps.
Alex M: starting manual traffic shift now — will reduce new session rate to us-east and failover to us-west. Running: 
```
# apply routing override
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/routing/override -d '{"route":"text-generation-prod","prefer_region":"us-west-2","drain_mode":"gradual"}'
```
Priya S: autoscaler logs show rapid pod restarts due to driver handshake failures. NVMe errors also on affected hosts. Raising a ticket with infra to isolate rack power rails.
Josh R: confirmed kernel panic pattern consistent with recent vendor driver update on that kernel. rolling back driver on a canary node.
SRE-Oncall: mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic to us-west and eu-west 2) throttle new sessions to reduce queue growth 3) node-level rollback of NIC driver 4) contact hardware ops for rack investigation.
Support-Escalation: opening high-touch case for 3 customers reporting errors; adding temporary credits and queue priority for their traffic in west region.
StatusBot: Status page updated (INC-2026-0233) — "Degraded capacity in us-east-1; routing to alternate regions; ETA ~45 minutes."
Alex M: traffic shift started at 1761284560. Observed 70% drop in 5xx within 90s for shifted routes.
Maya (support): posting this to support threads and sending templated note to affected customers now.
Ben L: keep top customers informed if ETA changes. Sales pinged.
Priya S: rollback completed on one canary host, it recovered and rejoined with healthy NIC. will iterate.
Josh R: workload throttles holding, token latency improved from 850ms -> 230ms on failover paths.
SRE-Oncall: marking as "mitigated" in the incident tracker. Root cause: vendor NIC driver regression combined with a rack-level hardware instability. Full remediation requires host driver rollback and hardware replacement for 4 hosts.
Alex M: next actions: schedule driver rollback across remaining hosts, coordinate with hardware ops for replacements, and draft postmortem. Please add any customer-facing follow-ups.
Maya (support): customers notified. will collect any escalations and share in #support-summary.
Ben L: flagging for postmortem action items: better preflight driver canary, automatic cross-region burst capacity, and clearer SLA communications for region failovers.
SRE-Oncall: thanks all — incident closed for customer-impacting state at 1761284699. Will own postmortem and timeline.
